text:
anya: Quick notes from today's speculative-decoding experiments on the quantized gptq-7b-v2 build. results look promising but we see some regressions on open-ended tasks. posting raw thread so we can iterate.
matt: TL;DR: throughput 1.7x median, up to 2.1x in favorably batched runs. quality delta: +0.2 ppl on LAMBADA, -1.5 BLEU on code summarization small set, human-fluency drop noticed on long-gen prompts.
lia: Can you paste the exact config + eval harness? need to reproduce. also what's the seed/temperature?
devon: ran with this command on r-runtime-canary: 
```bash
./run_infer --model gptq-7b-v2-q4f16 --speculative true --spec_stride 8 --spec_beam 2 --max_spec_len 32 --batch 8 --temp 0.8 --seed 42 
```
config snippet: 
```json
{"speculative": true, "spec_stride": 8, "spec_beam": 2, "max_spec_len": 32, "fallback": "sync", "kv_cache": true}
```
(dev note: quant backend = q4f16 w/ fused kernels)
matt: eval harness: 3 suites: LAMBADA (closed-book), CodeSum-200 (BLEU+ROUGE), and SummEval-100 (human-style proxies). all runs use greedy baseline + top-k sampling for speculative caller.
eval-bot: Automated eval summary (1719001400): {LAMBADA_ppl_delta: 0.20, CodeSum_BLEU_delta: -1.5, SummEval_ROUGE-L_delta: -0.9, Throughput_x: 1.73} (CI-flag: warn)
lia: Noted. The ppl increase on LAMBADA is small but BLEU drop worries me. Could be sampling mismatch — speculative decoding sometimes changes token distribution early which affects code tokens.
anya: Right. Hypothesis: quantization + early speculative prefixes cause wrong branch selection for tighter token distributions (code). We should test two controlled variants: (A) speculative on float baseline (no quant), (B) quantized w/o speculative, (C) quantized + speculative (current). Compare against beam search baseline for code tasks.
matt: Also observed occasional knee-case when KV cache gets a flush on spec fallback; latency spikes. Need to instrument reroute path. I added logs to runtime: 
```log
[spec] t=120ms fallback_reason=cache_miss prefix_len=18
[spec] t=450ms fallback_reason=policy_mismatch prefix_len=24
```
(devon: those correlate with batch boundaries)
lia: Proposed eval plan: 1) deterministic seeds, 200 prompts per suite, sample temps = [0.0,0.7,1.0], 2) measure exact match + n-gram + human proxy, 3) log token-level divergence between baseline and speculative.
anya: Good. Also add a quick ablation on max_spec_len = [8,16,32] and spec_beam = [1,2,4]. early signs show 8-16 preserve quality more.
devon: I'll queue runs on dedicated-canary GPU pool tonight and push metrics to /eng-ml/drive/spec-results. linking initial dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/spec-decoding/q4f16 (internal)
matt: If we can get throughput >=1.5x while keeping BLEU within -0.5 and human proxies within -0.3, we can include this as an opt-in optimization for Dedicated customers.
lia: I'll coordinate a small human annotation batch (n=150) for SummEval to verify fluency & factuality. Volunteers welcome.
anya: Thanks. For checklist: - devon: run ablations and upload logs - matt: add KV-cache instrumentation + fallback metrics - lia: run human eval + update pass/fail criteria - anya: draft rollout note + proposed canary gating
devon: on it. kicking off now, ETA ~12h. (reacts :rocket:)
eval-bot: CI job queued (job_id=spec-1719001234-ablate). will post final aggregated JSON when done.
anya: Nice. If results look good, we'll schedule a canary rollout with rollback policy = immediate fallback to non-speculative quant variant. cc @eng-runtime
matt: also add a regression alarm in Redwood Console: if BLEU drops >1.0 or SummEval proxy drops >0.7, auto-disable speculative per-route.
lia: Adding eval checklist to the doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/speculative-decoding-guidelines
anya: Perfect. we'll reconvene after the runs. :thumbsup:
